# JobQueue.push() method

Enqueues one job, optionally delayed or time-limited, refusing to enqueue without a handler.

**Signature:**

```typescript
push(job: T, options?: PushOptions): JobQueue<T>;
```

**Returns:**

[JobQueue](/api/job/latest/job.jobqueue/)<!-- -->&lt;T&gt;

this queue, for chaining

## Exceptions

TypeError if no handler has been registered with [JobQueue.onPop()](/api/job/latest/job.jobqueue.onpop/)

## Remarks

The handler check is the only difference from [JobQueuePublisher.push()](/api/job/latest/job.jobqueuepublisher.push/)<!-- -->, whose caveats all apply here too — most importantly that a successful call means the job was handed off, not that the broker accepted it. A broker failure is logged, not thrown.
